---
title: Security
description: What a build reads, writes and never does, surface by surface, with the file in the source that decides each.
---

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components'

```js
// @generated by loclizr abi=1. Do not edit; run `loclizr build`.
```

Every file the build may delete starts with that line, and that is the shape of this whole page:
each surface is bounded by something you can read in `packages/loclizr/src`, and the file is
named beside each claim. Nothing here describes a policy. There is no policy yet, and the last
section says so.

## What a build reads

| Input | Where | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Catalogs | the `catalogs` pattern, `locales/{locale}.json` by default | Parsed as JSON. Never written. |
| Translator notes | `meta`, `locales/en.meta.json` by default | Parsed as JSON. |
| The config | `loclizr.config.ts` or `--config` | Executed as code, see below. |
| Your sources | `scan.include`, `src/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,mts,mjs}` by default | Read into memory for the usage scan (`src/scan/index.ts`), never written, never executed. |
| The existing tree and record | `outDir` and `record` | Read to compare bytes, so unchanged files are not rewritten and `check` can report staleness. |

`loclizr.config.ts` is executed, in the build's own process, through `jiti`
(`src/config/index.ts`), with whatever it imports. That is the same trust a `vite.config.ts`
carries: a config file you did not write is code you did not review.

## What it writes and deletes

`build` writes files under `outDir`, each starting with the header above, plus one `.gitignore`
written only when absent. The record goes to `record`, `locales/loclizr.context.json` by default.
Every build write lands in a temporary file beside the target and is renamed into place
(`src/compiler/output.ts`). `init` writes `loclizr.config.ts` and `locales/en.json` with the `wx`
flag, so an existing file is never overwritten (`src/cli/init.ts`). `check` writes nothing.

The prune deletes a file only when it sits under `outDir`, carries the header, and this emit did
not produce it. A file without the header is left where it is and reported as `LZ1021`. The
sweep collects regular files only: a symbolic link under `outDir` is neither read, overwritten
nor deleted.

## What it never does

- No network. loclizr's own code opens no socket, and the built entries import only
  `node:async_hooks`, `node:crypto`, `node:fs/promises`, `node:path` and `node:util` from Node.
  A search of its seven production packages for the network and child-process modules finds none.
- No telemetry and no update check, for the same reason.
- No child processes.
- Environment: loclizr's own code reads `NODE_ENV`, to drop its development warnings, and
  `NO_COLOR`. Three dependencies read their own: `jiti` its `JITI_*` variables and `TMPDIR`,
  plus `NODE_ENV`, `DEBUG`, `NODE_DEBUG` and `BABEL_*` through the Babel it bundles for
  transforms; `picocolors` the colour conventions `FORCE_COLOR`, `NO_COLOR`, `TERM` and `CI`;
  `tinyglobby` `TINYGLOBBY_DEBUG`.

## Dependency surface

The entry an app ships, `loclizr`, imports nothing outside its own files. `loclizr/react` adds
`react`, an optional peer; `loclizr/server` adds `node:async_hooks`. The compiler and CLI carry
the production dependencies, which the browser never sees:

| Direct | Pulls in | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@formatjs/icu-messageformat-parser` | `@formatjs/icu-skeleton-parser` | Parsing ICU at build time |
| `jiti` | | Loading a TypeScript config |
| `picocolors` | | Colour in the human reporter |
| `tinyglobby` | `fdir`, `picomatch` | Expanding `scan.include` |

`typescript` is a development dependency only: declarations are printed as text.

## Catalog text cannot become code

Every catalog value that reaches a generated template literal passes through `templateText` in
`src/emit/shared.ts`, which escapes backslash, backtick, `$`, carriage return, newline and the
two Unicode line separators. A value ending in `$` beside an argument would otherwise join into a
live interpolation, which is why every `$` is escaped rather than only `${`. Keys and option
values go through `quoted`, and the `.d.ts` doc comment escapes `*/` so a source string cannot
close it early. A catalog can put any text into a string literal and nothing into an expression.

## Path containment

`outDir` must resolve inside the project root. The config check is lexical (`LZ1007`, exit 2,
`src/config/resolve.ts`), and `src/compiler/output.ts` checks again at write time through
`realpath`: an `outDir` that is a link to somewhere outside the project, or a link one level down
such as `outDir/messages`, stops the write with `LZ5001` and nothing under it is pruned. The
prune's own list never follows a link either, because the header alone cannot prove the build
wrote whatever a link points at.

## Hostile headers and cookies

Nothing a request carries reaches the response unmatched. `localeFromHeaders` and `negotiate`
(`src/server/index.ts`) resolve the cookie and every `Accept-Language` range through
`matchLocale` (`src/runtime/store.ts`), which returns a tag from the declared list or the source
locale, and only that value goes into `Content-Language` and the request scope. The client reads
its cookie through the same matcher, and reads `<html lang>` only when it is shaped like a tag.

## Terminal escapes in diagnostics

Keys, source text, descriptions and paths all print through one sanitizer in
`src/diagnostics/index.ts`: every C0 control except tab and the deliberate newline, plus DEL and
the C1 block, prints as `<U+XX>`. A catalog holding an ANSI sequence cannot erase a diagnostic
already printed or plant an OSC 8 hyperlink in a CI log. The JSON reporter escapes DEL and C1 as
`\uXXXX`, which a parser decodes back losslessly.

## Not covered

- No CSP guidance. The generated code is plain modules with no inline script, so there is
  nothing for a policy to allow, and this page makes no claim beyond that.
- The locale cookie is written without `Secure` and without `Domain`, with `path=/`,
  `SameSite=Lax` and a one year `max-age`; only its name is configurable. It cannot be `HttpOnly`,
  because `setLocale` writes it from the browser.
- The config file is code. Review it like any other build script.
